proposed_value: 10,500-square-foot plastics processing laboratory in the Jack Burke Research and Economic Development Center (opened 2006), described by the college as the largest undergraduate plastics processing lab of its type in the country: ten microprocessor-controlled injection molding machines (17-200 tons; Arburg, Boy, Cincinnati Milacron, Demag, Engel, Ferromatik, Husky, Sumitomo, VanDorn), extrusion and injection blow molding (Bekum, Jomar), single- and twin-screw extrusion (Davis Standard, Killion, CW Brabender, Wayne, Steer; strand, pipe and sheet dies), thermoforming machines (Formech 660; MAAC ASP 30x30), a blown film tower, a 75-ton Loranger compression molding press, and a material testing/measurement suite (capillary, torque and dual-bore capillary rheometers, DSC, Flash DSC, TGA, DMA, Bruker Vertex FTIR, universal testing machines).

10,500-square-foot plastics processing laboratory in the Jack Burke Research and Economic Development Center (opened 2006), described by the college as the largest undergraduate plastics processing lab of its type in the country: ten microprocessor-controlled injection molding machines (17-200 tons; Arburg, Boy, Cincinnati Milacron, Demag, Engel, Ferromatik, Husky, Sumitomo, VanDorn), extrusion and injection blow molding (Bekum, Jomar), single- and twin-screw extrusion (Davis Standard, Killion, CW Brabender, Wayne, Steer; strand, pipe and sheet dies), thermoforming machines (Formech 660; MAAC ASP 30x30), a blown film tower, a 75-ton Loranger compression molding press, and a material testing/measurement suite (capillary, torque and dual-bore capillary rheometers, DSC, Flash DSC, TGA, DMA, Bruker Vertex FTIR, universal testing machines).

Industry-driven labs with industrial-scale process equipment across five major plastics processes (extrusion, injection molding, blow molding, thermoforming, rotational molding) and extensive material testing laboratories; campus also hosts the Shell Polymers Rotational Molding Center of Excellence.
